items.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: Leonard Feather came to hear me play one time... he decided to record me for United Artists and Leonard was in the middle of it, and that was my first major recording. The album was called “Bird Calls”

ctx.x: When was your first opportunity to record?

My first opportunity to record was in 1962 I believe. Leonard Feather came to hear me play one time. He was very impressed with my playing. And then Art Blakey, my former husband, Richie Goldberg, was a drummer, and he knew all the musicians from back east, and when he came out here, we married out here and everybody would end up at our house one time or the other for me to fix spaghetti and chili and stuff. But anyway, that’s when I met Art Blakey. And Art Blakey asked me to come and sit in with him one night.…
major recording. The album was called “Bird Calls” it’s a collector’s item now, whatever that means.
